description.value: An fMRI study examined how fear and disgust propensity and sensitivity relate to emotion-specific brain activation in healthy women viewing affective pictures.

value: We hypothesized that subjects high in disgust propensity and fear propensity would show increased activity in such brain areas involved in the processing of primary emotions (e.g. amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex, insula).

Based on previous research we expected that disgust sensitivity and anxiety sensitivity are negatively correlated with the activation of the parietal cortex and prefrontal cognitive control areas (dorsomedial, dorsolateral).

description.value: The Questionnaire for the Assessment of Disgust Sensitivity (QADS) assessed disgust propensity, defined as proneness to feel disgust in specific contexts. It comprised 37 items scored from 0 (not disgusting) to 4 (very disgusting); total scores ranged from 0 to 4 and had a sample mean of 2.3 (SD 0.6).

description.value: The Disgust Sensitivity Scale, a subscale of the revised Disgust Propensity and Sensitivity Scale (DPSS-R), assessed the cognitive evaluation of disgust experiences and perceived negative consequences of feeling disgusted. It comprised 8 items scored from 1 (never) to 5 (always), with scores ranging from 4 to 20 and a sample mean of 15.1 (SD 3.5).
